title: The arch of a footbridge
body: A town is building a small footbridge over a canal. The engineer draws the underside of the arch on graph paper with the road level along the x-axis, both axes in metres. The curve of the arch is modelled by y = p(x), where p(x) = -x² + 2x + 8. The arch rises above the road and comes down to meet the road level at two points, which are the feet of the arch. Recall that the points where the graph of y = p(x) meets the x-axis have as their x-coordinates exactly the zeroes of p(x).
